text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- China sends 40-strong advance party of People's Liberation Army to Hongkong in preparation for Chinese soldiers who will be stationed in from July 1.
- Unemployed man severely burnt when a portable LPG gas cylinder explodes in one-room flat in Marsiling.
- Inder Kumar Gujral sworn in as India's 12th prime minister, ending country's three weeks of turmoil and intrigue.
- 86-year old American tourist who did not show up at wedding to which invited found locked and alive in motel in Sydney after going missing for three days.
- Singapore's non-oil domestic exports, a key indicator of the health of Singapore's export-driven economy, drop 2.1 percent, less than-expected.
- Three Singaporeans among world's top 50 career women listed in Euromoney.
- Price of residential property in Tokyo still world's highest, 45 times more than in New York and 14 times greater than in London.
- Indonesia freezes negotations with Japan on controversial national car project after Tokyo decides to refer issue to World Trade Organisation.
- Market share of Mercedes-Benz parallel importers shrink for the first time since 1994.
- Diversified construction services group Poh Lian Holdings expected to launch initial public offering in Stock Exchange of Singapore at end of month.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore gives approval to Popular Book Company for mainboard listing in which company expected to float 60 to 80 million shares at below Singapore $1 apiece.
- Natsteel shares rise sharply to Singapore $4 apiece, causing total of 6.21 million shares changed hands.
- PC maker Packard Bell-NEC orders of Aztech System sound cards not hit despite company's decision to use Creative Technology's sound cards.
